newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Publicis in US$250 mln spree - chairman.
newsitem.headline: Publicis in US$250 mln spree - chairman.

text.p: The chairman of French advertising group Publicis SA said on Tuesday the company planned to spend US$250 million on acquisitions to turn itself into a global player in the media world.
"We have US$250 million to spend on acquisitions," Publicis chairman Maurice Levy told Reuters in an interview.
Levy, speaking after a news conference to announce taking a 60 percent controlling stake in Singapore advertising agency Eureka, said he planned an accelerated acquisitions strategy.
"We want to spend this money before the end of 1998," he said.
Levy said he hoped to have announced "five or six" more deals in Asia by the end of June. He said Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand posed interesting opportunities.

Levy said the purchasing programme began in August 1996 with a deal to take control of the Paulino Romero y Asociados agency in Mexico. He said Publicis was looking to strengthen its South American presence in Argentina, Venezuela and Chile.
